summary: Infrastructure-weighted, game-loop-aware live audit after Session 85 exhausted 3/3 primary items and 36/36 innovations. Four new premises survive direct code review. Dynasty Story is an exposed authenticated mutation that accepts browser-authored clan identity and outcomes, has no production caller, and can append to any clan. Tournament advancement trusts a creator-entered winner while every bracket match retains gameId=null and consumes no result certificate. PlayerStatsStore truncates and reconstructs leaderboard_cache inside every certified match transaction. Rival Challenge progress is written to localStorage from client activity events even though the attested match-stat spine can carry the same deterministic rivalry evidence. External release gates remain evidence corridors, not implementation claims.

sample.method: Targeted live-code and contract survey; sample-codebase and studio-oracle helpers are absent, so premises were manually traced across registration, store, schema, client, attestation, and executable contract surfaces.

nextMoves: Make competitive brackets consume the same certified result authority as progression.

items.axis: security / artificial intelligence / token reduction / retention
items.title: Turn Dynasty Story into a certificate-bound clan chronicle
items.why: POST /api/vaultfront/dynasty-story accepts clanId, clanName, outcomes, and moments from any resolved identity, then appends generated text to that clan. It does not prove clan membership or match participation, consumes no result certificate, and has no client caller. A durable public history can therefore be fabricated or poisoned.
items.coreLoopStep: certified clan participant → completed match → tamper-evident dynasty chapter
items.recipe: Replace the browser-authored mutation with an extracted DynastyChronicleRouter accepting only gameId. Resolve the verified actor, archived result certificate, participant record, and authoritative clan membership; derive canonical inputs from the record; create a canonical AI evidence/response receipt; append at most once per clan/game behind a database uniqueness constraint; expose receipt metadata with the story; wire WinModal to request the current certified chapter; bind the route into both policy surfaces; cover outsider, nonparticipant, wrong clan, replay, tamper, duplicate, provider failure, and process-local posture.

L1.recipe: Reject claimed clan/outcome fields and require the actor to belong to the requested clan.

L2.recipe: Accept only gameId, derive clan/outcomes from an archived result certificate, and deduplicate clan/game writes.

L3.recipe: Extract the router, create canonical request/response receipts, persist a certificate- and evidence-bound event exactly once, expose structured provenance, wire the post-match caller, and ratchet route/composition policy.

items.title: Make every tournament advancement consume a certified match result
items.why: Tournament report accepts creator-entered winnerId. TournamentMatch.gameId is initialized null and never assigned, so bracket advancement, completion, and downstream competitive meaning are not tied to an actual match or its certificate.
items.coreLoopStep: seeded pairing → bound private match → certified winner → idempotent bracket advancement
items.recipe: Extract a TournamentRouter and a pure TournamentResultAuthority. Change reporting to accept gameId only; load the archived GameRecord and verify its result certificate; map certificate client IDs to persistent participants; require exact bracket participant and map identity; derive the winner server-side; store gameId plus certificateId atomically; reject reuse across matches and duplicate/conflicting reports; persist errors rather than silently claiming success; bind result-certificate evidence in route policy; and cover byes, wrong players, wrong map, invalid certificate, team-shaped result, replay, restart hydration, and concurrent reports.

L1.recipe: Require a gameId and derive the winner from a verified archived certificate.

L2.recipe: Bind exact participants/map, persist game and certificate identity, and reject duplicate game reuse.

L3.recipe: Extract router and pure authority seams, add transactional/idempotent persistence and hydration, enforce route policy, and cover adversarial plus concurrent advancement.

items.title: Remove table-wide leaderboard work from the certified match transaction
items.why: PlayerStatsStore.pgRecordMatch truncates leaderboard_cache and inserts up to 1,000 ranked rows before COMMIT for every certified game. Concurrent matches serialize behind table-wide writes, while a cache failure can roll back otherwise valid progression.
items.coreLoopStep: certified match fan-out → durable player stats → independently fresh ranked read
items.recipe: Make player_stats the sole write authority. Replace per-match TRUNCATE/INSERT with an indexed top-N ranking projection on read or a versioned refresh coordinator outside the correctness transaction; preserve deterministic tie ordering and placement exclusion; publish projection source/freshness; make the memory and Postgres paths semantically identical; retire or migrate the stale cache without destructive launch assumptions; and test no table-wide query occurs during recordMatch, ties, empty state, idempotent replay, concurrent games, and read failure isolation.

L1.recipe: Move the cache rebuild after COMMIT so cache failure cannot roll back progression.

L2.recipe: Replace the cache with an indexed deterministic top-N projection and add parity tests.

L3.recipe: Ship a versioned projection contract with stable tie order, source/freshness metadata, migration-safe retirement, concurrent-write tests, and direct query-shape assertions.

items.title: Make Rival Challenge a signed revenge projection from deterministic simulation
items.why: ControlPanel stores rivalry revenge in localStorage after client-observed activity updates, and WinModal trusts that value to render and instrument the retention challenge. The browser can fabricate, lose, or replay progress independently of the attested match result.
items.coreLoopStep: enemy intercept → deterministic counter-intercept → signed revenge evidence → rematch challenge
items.recipe: Track the last convoy interceptor per victim inside deterministic VaultFrontExecution; increment a rivalryRevenge stat only when the victim later intercepts that same opponent; add the metric to Stats and StatsSchemas so quorum and MatchResultCertificate bind it; remove the localStorage authority; have WinModal derive the challenge from current signed allPlayersStats; keep storage only for non-authoritative next-goal preference; add ordering, wrong-rival, repeated-cycle, serialization, certificate-tamper, and browser-reload coverage; preserve all balance values.

L1.recipe: Put the revenge counter in deterministic match stats and render it directly.

L2.recipe: Track opponent identity and prove only a counter-intercept against the same rival increments.

L3.recipe: Bind the metric through simulation, schema, quorum certificate, recap, telemetry, and adversarial tests while deleting browser authority.
